workflowDefinitions.name: UweDesignWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Creates or refines a well-specified GitHub issue with multi-agent consensus review, then gates on CEO design-approval. Consensus loop (max 3 rounds) — if exhausted or needs_human_review, escalates to CEO gate instead of cancelling. CEO wait loop (hourly reminders, no auto-cancel). Returns {IssueNumber: N} on approval. Replaces compiled DesignWorkflow. Epic grants (#436): the author outputs BODY_SHA256, consensus attests it (author and CTO excluded), it is published as ReviewRef only after a unanimous attested approval, the design gate is visit-guarded, and a grant decision re-hashes the issue body (verify_approved_body) and fails with ERROR:approved_artifact_changed on a mismatch. Human approvals skip the re-hash.

{{vars.consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

Incorporate this prior CEO feedback (if any):
{{vars.approval_signal.Comment | default: 'none'}}

{{vars.ceo_consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

At the end of your response, output exactly: ISSUE_NUMBER: <number>
After your last edit, also output the SHA-256 of the issue body bytes on its own line, computed with `gh issue view <number> --repo {{input.Repo}} --json body | jq -j .body | sha256sum` (first field):
BODY_SHA256: <64-hex>

- A 'Files to Touch' section enumerating each file/path the implementer will modify.
- An 'Acceptance Criteria' section with testable assertions (not vague goals).
- A 'Constraints / MUST NOT' section listing at least 3 domain-specific dangers the implementation must avoid. Not generic boilerplate — concrete, workflow-specific MUST-NOTs.

workflowDefinitions.name: UweDocMaintenanceWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Post-merge documentation maintenance (#436): prepare (read-only artifact with ARTIFACT_SHA256), deterministic classify (only memory and repo_doc targets are delegable), consensus review of the exact artifact (PrepAgent and CTO excluded; skipped without ConsensusAgents), publish ReviewRef only after a unanimous attested approval of a delegable artifact, a visit-guarded doc-review gate, then apply exactly the approved artifact and check APPLIED_ARTIFACT_SHA256. Nothing is written before the gate. Max 2 rounds. Inputs: Repo, PrNumber, BranchName, MergeSummary, optional IssueNumber, ConsensusAgents and PrepAgent (empty → the CTO, which makes the gate human-only).

steps.name: prepare
steps.instruction:
Prepare the documentation changes for merged PR #{{input.PrNumber}} on branch `{{input.BranchName}}` in repo {{input.Repo}}.

This step READS ONLY. Do not write fleet-memory, project contexts, instructions, repository files, branches or PRs. Nothing is written before the doc-review gate; after approval exactly the artifact you return is applied.

Merge summary: {{input.MergeSummary}}

Gate feedback on the previous artifact (if any):
{{vars.doc_review | default: 'none'}}

Review feedback on the previous artifact (if any):
{{vars.doc_consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

Steps:
1. Fetch the diff: `gh pr diff {{input.PrNumber}} --repo {{input.Repo}}`
2. Decide whether any documentation must change: architecture, config, ports, services, schemas, tool mappings, docker config, CI/CD or infrastructure, as described in fleet-memory entries (including 'WorkflowType — operational context' memories), repository docs, project contexts or agent instructions.
3. If nothing must change, output exactly the line: PREP: NO_DOC
4. Otherwise output, in this order:
PREP: ARTIFACT
TARGET: <type> <id>   (one line per target; type is memory, repo_doc, project_context or instruction; id is the memory id or 'new', owner/repo:path, the context name or the instruction name)
ARTIFACT_SHA256: <64-hex>
-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----
<the complete new content for every target, each section headed by its TARGET line>
-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----

The artifact hash is the SHA-256 of the artifact body: every line strictly between the two marker lines, each terminated by a single LF, UTF-8. Compute it with:
awk '/^-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=1;next}/^-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=0}f' <file> | sha256sum

steps.name: apply
steps.instruction:
The doc-review gate approved the documentation artifact for PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in {{input.Repo}}. Apply EXACTLY the artifact below — nothing else and no extra edits.

Prepared output (the artifact is between the marker lines):
{{vars.prep_result}}

For each TARGET:
- memory: memory_store / memory_update with exactly the artifact content.
- repo_doc: open a PR with exactly the artifact content for that path, then merge it (squash).
- project_context: update_project_context with exactly the artifact content.
- instruction: update_instruction with exactly the artifact content, then reprovision_agent for each agent that uses it.

Then recompute the hash of the artifact you applied. The artifact hash is the SHA-256 of the artifact body: every line strictly between the two marker lines, each terminated by a single LF, UTF-8. Compute it with:
awk '/^-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=1;next}/^-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=0}f' <file> | sha256sum

Output exactly one line with it:
APPLIED_ARTIFACT_SHA256: <64-hex>

steps.name: pin
steps.instruction:
REQUIRE_ACCEPTANCE: {{vars.acceptance_mode}}
In off mode read only the actual gh headRefOid, EVERY page of check-runs and commit statuses for ci-rollup (zero/error is pending), and diff paths for change-class (deny list wins). Return HEAD_OID, CI and CHANGE_CLASS only. Skip issue-body hashing, design lookup, plan, receipts, prior rounds, owner and capability-map checks. Ignore all acceptance tokens even if present. Do not run acceptance work. The instructions below apply only in required mode.

workflowDefinitions.name: UweCarteBlancheWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Bounded epic reconciliation with wake-only signals, explicit failed-tick repair and independent completion review; existing running definitions are unchanged.

steps.name: epic_tick
steps.instruction:
Epic {{input.EpicRepo}}#{{input.EpicIssue}}. Read the issue body, not its whole comment trail.

The tick stays short (one or two minutes), never waits in the background, and never reads the whole comment trail. It must contain, in substance:

1. **Header:** `Woken by: {{vars.wake_kind}} from {{vars.wake_ref}}.` `timeout` means a scheduled check. Anything else is a hint: check that run's real status first. A wake never approves, rejects or ends anything. The header also carries the previous tick's values:
   - `Previous updatedAt: {{vars.epic_seen | default:'none'}}`
   - `Previous fingerprint: {{vars.epic_fingerprint}}`
   - `Previous status: {{vars.tick_status | default:'none'}}`
   - `Previous next action: {{vars.epic_next}}`
   - `Previous ask: {{vars.tick_ask | default:'none'}}`
   - `Last completion review: {{vars.epic_consensus.FinalVerdict | default:'none'}}`
   - `Last completion findings: {{vars.completion_findings | default:'none'}}` (authoritative, full, never truncated; set only on the `changes_requested` path, see §3.6)
   - `Findings write: {{vars.findings_write_status}}` (`completed`, or `unknown`/`failed`/`incomplete` when the checklist write did not finish; `none` before any review)
2. **Step 0:** `curl -s -m 60 {{config.OrchestratorUrl}}/api/epic-drivers/{{workflow.id}}/state`. End the tick early **only** when all of these hold:
   - the issue `updatedAt` is unchanged;
   - `fingerprint` equals `{{vars.epic_fingerprint}}`;
   - `errors` is empty and `truncated` is false;
   - **no child has a non-empty `gateVisit`** (parked at any gate, whether `cto_decide` or `human_decide`) and no child is `terminal_failed`;
   - the previous status is not `none` (the first tick and the tick after a failed tick never end early);
   - the previous status is not `proposed`. A tick after a completion review never ends early. It fully reconciles against `Last completion findings`, which are authoritative. When `Findings write` is not `completed`, or the checklist lacks a finding, the tick writes the missing findings to the checklist itself. It reports `proposed` again only with fresh per-criterion evidence that every finding is resolved.

   **An early exit re-emits the previous tick's `EPIC_STATUS`, `EPIC_NEXT_ACTION` and `EPIC_ASK` unchanged**, with `EPIC_STATE_CHANGED: no`, the observed `EPIC_SEEN` and `EPIC_FINGERPRINT`, and a fresh `EPIC_NEXT_TICK_AT`. It never reports `working` unless the previous tick did. A parked or failed child is never progress: every tick with one does the full reconcile, and reports `blocked` when the gate is the only remaining work. If the state cannot be read, do a full read and do not end early.
3. **Reconcile** as today: read only what changed, establish real state (merged, CI, alive, deployed), act, and update the checklist only with evidence. Keep each child workflow id in the checklist row it belongs to.
   - **Partial state.** When the state reply has non-empty `errors` (`deadline`, `candidates_incomplete`, `candidates_page_failed`, `linkage_unknown:…`, `children_truncated`, a Temporal error), or cannot be read at all, the children list is **partial**.
     - A child missing from a partial list is **unknown, not absent**. Do not mark its row done or failed from the state reply.
     - Never report `proposed` from a partial list. Report `working`, with `EPIC_NEXT_ACTION: system:state-partial:<first error>`.
     - Start nothing for an affected row unless the complete §8 duplicate check proves no Running owner. If that check errors or is incomplete, start nothing.
4. **Child outcomes** come from the state endpoint, never from a status alone:
   - a design child counts as approved **only** when its `outcome` is `approved` and its `outcomeIssue` is the issue the tick expects for that row;
   - `not_approved`, `invalid_result`, `failed`, `unknown` and `no_result` never count as approved;
   - a Completed `UweDesignToPrWorkflow` is never evidence by itself, because it returns no result: use its linked design child's `outcome` and its PR child's real merge state;
   - a PR child counts as merged only when `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` shows `MERGED` with a non-null `mergedAt`.
5. **`cto_decide`:** if `TargetAgent` is the configured CTO agent, run the existing epic-grant decision procedure once (`docs/epic-grants.md`: an independent check of the exact artifact, one send, no retry; read the grant's decisions first). Otherwise call `notify_cto` with the gate, run and visit.
6. **Dispatch (unchanged legacy rule):** do or dispatch the next actionable step the epic already authorizes. If some steps are blocked but others are actionable, do the actionable ones and report `working`. Before any start, run the owner selection and duplicate check in §8, and pass input `WaiterWorkflowId={{workflow.id}}`. Autonomous charter dispatch (only when state grants[] shows an active mode=autonomous grant; otherwise keep the legacy dispatch rule):
- Read that grant's immutable scope and plan using GET /api/epic-grants/<id>; never create, revoke, edit or widen a grant. Before EVERY start call {{config.OrchestratorUrl}}/api/epic-grants/<id>/admission?workflowType=<type>&repo=<repo>&issue=<number-or-empty>&planItem=<id>, then perform the existing duplicate-owner check. Only result=admit permits a start. An error, incomplete visibility, or deny starts nothing and records its reason in the checklist.
- Attempt ids are <Type>-<repo-name>-<plan-id>-d<first8-driver-run-id>-a<n>, n=1..3, with id_reuse_policy=reject_duplicate. Describe each exact attempt. Retry automatically ONLY after Failed or TimedOut. Canceled, Terminated, Completed without a done outcome, unknown/missing history, or the third failed attempt never redispatch: record needs-authority with reason attempt_canceled, attempt_terminated, attempt_completed_not_done, attempt_status_unknown, or attempts_exhausted respectively. Never reset or reuse an attempt id.
- For each held item write EPIC_NEXT_ACTION: human:charter:<reason>:<plan-id> and one EPIC_ASK sentence naming the needed human decision. Keep the attempt ids and actual statuses in that item's checklist row.
- Every child input carries WaiterWorkflowId={{workflow.id}}. Design and DesignToPr receive AutonomyGrantId=<grant-id>; PR and DesignToPr receive RequireAcceptance=true. No running child or open PR for the same target may be replaced.
- An item is done only from exact evidence: design outcome=approved with matching issue, PR state=MERGED and non-null mergedAt, DesignToPr's linked design AND PR both done. A Completed status alone never means done. Null-issue CREATE items require a returned positive issue recorded for that plan row; mismatched/unpinned results remain unknown.
- Ready means not done/excluded, every after dependency done, no Running attempt, fewer than three attempts and admission=admit. Walk ready items in plan order and start at most TWO per tick. If more are ready, request one self more-ready wake using the existing wake protocol; add no wait, sleep or background watcher.
- working means something is in flight or was started; blocked only when all remaining items wait on human gates, never because of a parked doc-review; needs-authority when all remaining items need a new charter/human decision. Use the exact attempt reasons above for failed retry eligibility. Preserve all existing independent review, one-send gate procedures and human authority boundaries.

7. **Status choice:**
   - `working`: something is in flight or was started.
   - `blocked`: every remaining item waits on a human gate.
   - `needs-authority`: every remaining item needs new authority (out of scope, or a design child that is not approved).
   - `proposed`: every item is done, the state reply is complete (empty `errors`), and evidence is cited per acceptance criterion.
8. **Report lines**, last and in this order:
   - `EPIC_SEEN: <updatedAt>`
   - `EPIC_CHILD: <one running child id|none>`
   - `EPIC_STATUS: working|blocked|needs-authority|proposed`
   - `EPIC_STATE_CHANGED: yes|no`
   - `EPIC_NEXT_TICK_AT: <UTC>`: working = now + 31 min, blocked or needs-authority = now + 61 min, proposed = `review-now`. Notify time and storm cooldowns are excluded; a wake may come sooner.
   - `EPIC_FINGERPRINT: <fingerprint|none>`
   - `EPIC_NEXT_ACTION: <owner>:<action>:<ref>`, e.g. `cto:decide:merge-approval:2@<workflow-id>` or `human:approve:<what>`
   - `EPIC_ASK: <one sentence, the exact human action>`, for `blocked` or `needs-authority`
   - `EPIC_BLOCKER: <workflow id|none>`, informational

   `EPIC_STATE_CHANGED: yes` only when a checklist item completed or failed, a child started or ended, the status changed, human action became necessary, or completion is proposed. The first tick is `yes`; byte counts, percentages and ETAs alone are `no`.


Owner selection and duplicate check:

Fields come from unauthenticated orchestrator GETs:

| field | endpoint |
|---|---|
| `agentName`, `role`, `effectiveStatus`, `isDbOnly` | `GET /api/agents` |
| `provider`, `tools[].toolName` + `tools[].isEnabled`, `projects`, `envRefs` | `GET /api/agents/{name}/config` |

Every comparison is an exact, case-sensitive ordinal match. "Enabled tools" means the `toolName` values with `isEnabled == true`.

1. The named owner N is usable when `effectiveStatus == "idle"` and `isDbOnly == false`.
2. Otherwise pick an agent C that meets **every** rule. N's `/config` is read even when N is DB-only or not provisioned.
   - `C.role == N.role`;
   - `C.effectiveStatus == "idle"` and `C.isDbOnly == false`;
   - `C.projects` ⊇ `N.projects`;
   - C's enabled tools ⊇ N's enabled tools;
   - `C.envRefs` ⊇ `N.envRefs` (every env ref);
   - C is not the configured CTO, not the driver's `TargetAgent`, and not in that workflow's `ConsensusAgents`;
   - no Running workflow already owns the same target issue.

   Tie-break: `C.provider == N.provider` first, then `agentName` ascending (ordinal).
3. If N's `/config` cannot be read, report `blocked` and ask the human to provision N or name an owner.
4. Record `owner=C (replaces N: <effectiveStatus>) verified <UTC>` in the checklist row.
5. If no agent qualifies, report `blocked` with that exact human action.
6. Never create, update or reprovision agents, and never write tools, projects, instructions or grants.

**Duplicate check before any start:** list Running workflows and open linked PRs for the target repo and issue. If one exists, record it and start nothing. The check is **complete** only when both lists return without error and the workflow list is not truncated: `temporal_list_workflows` with `query` `ExecutionStatus="Running" AND Repo="<repo>" AND IssueNumber=<n>` and `limit` 100 returns fewer than 100 rows, and `gh pr list --repo <repo> --state open --search "<n>"` succeeds. Any error or a full page means incomplete: start nothing (fail-closed).

steps.name: pre_stage
steps.instruction: Before any action, enforce the lease: if now is later than {{input.PinnedAt}} + {{input.MaxDurationSeconds}} seconds or a verified cleanup receipt already exists for {{input.AttemptId}}, create nothing and return STAGE_RESULT: env_blocked / REASON: attempt_expired. Read the actual PR head and require {{input.HeadOid}}, otherwise create nothing and return head_changed. Use only the approved plan at sha256 {{input.PlanSha256}} for {{input.Repo}} PR {{input.PrNumber}}. No new privileges, configuration, instructions, definitions, deployment, providers or production effects beyond the explicit plan. Owner-stage work is one attempt with no retries. Run exactly stage {{vars.stage_kind}}:{{vars.stage_index}}, then end the turn. Pre stage one confirms every capability and prerequisite before resources: use the validated SshTargets {{input.SshTargets}} and capability map {{input.CapabilityMapCommit}} / {{input.CapabilityMapSha256}}, report names only, never credential values. The plan's pre/post stage lists decide done, never choose a wait or create a schedule. Preserve isolation/resources/checks on HarnessRetry={{input.HarnessRetry}}; save any harness diff. Write a new immutable protected receipt with attempt, PR, head, source archive/image/map/plan hashes, commands, exit codes, actual HTTP counts, timestamps, lease/deadline, baseline, isolation, owned resources, cleanup, and harness_retry. Post only acceptance_plan.py render-comment output after its fail-closed scrub, best effort. Never return a pass for an unrun check.

steps.instruction: Check the lease and cleanup receipt first, but expired attempts still permit idempotent cleanup only, never stage work. Otherwise remove only resources labelled fleet.acceptance.attempt={{input.AttemptId}}, compare the immutable baseline, and save a new protected cleanup receipt.
